sections.description: The talk opens by illustrating how Land's End achieves high reliability (phone response before dialing, 24-hour shipping) as the platform that enables a differentiated customer experience beyond mere product.
sections.title: Reliability as the foundation for customer experience

sections.description: Bliss describes extending care to the kids line by printing animal heads/tails inside the box to foster an emotional connection and shared family values, illustrating how small touches can humanize a brand.
sections.title: Emotional connection through branding and packaging

sections.description: Bliss recommends embedding five customer-focused questions into executive discourse, especially asking who the newest and who the lost customers are, and iterating based on ongoing customer feedback to keep customer focus embedded in strategy.
sections.title: Customer math: five questions and ongoing feedback

sections.description: Illustrates how Zappos lets staff solve problems and trust customers, including generous return policies, creating loyal customers and word-of-mouth growth.
sections.title: Zappos as a model of frontline trust

sections.description: Bliss outlines three operating principles that define successful beloved brands: clear purpose, passionate culture, and empowering people, reinforcing that culture drives behavior beyond strict rules.
sections.title: Beloved companies: clarity, passion, and people-driven culture

sections.description: The speaker cites Genentech’s rigorous cultural screening and 1-800-GOT-JUNK’s branding and service standards, illustrating how purpose and culture translate into measurable customer experiences.
sections.title: Examples of culture in action: Genentech, 1-800-GOT-JUNK, and more

concepts: impact of positive call experiences on repeat business
silobusting to protect the customer journey
sections.description: Bliss emphasizes that frontline agents preserve the brand with every interaction and provides data (86% repurchase after positive calls) to illustrate the business value of good service and the risk of siloed failures.
sections.title: Frontline as brand preservation and the cost of poor experiences

sections.description: The speaker argues for uniting leadership across functions to deliver a unified customer experience, coining the 'stairway to desire' as a metaphor for building stronger customer loyalty through collaboration and shared metrics.
sections.title: Silos, alignment, and the ladder to desire

summary: Jeanne Bliss discusses how leading organizations move beyond silos to design holistic, customer-centric experiences. She emphasizes reliability as the foundation for trust (e.g., Land’s End shipping within 24 hours, responsive service), then explains how emotional connection—such as packaging that speaks to shared values—can differentiate brands. The talk frames customer-centric leadership around the practice of 'customer math' (tracking new and lost customers, gathering regular feedback), frontline empowerment (trusting staff to do the right thing, exemplified by Zappos), and a culture built on clear purpose, passion, and consistent behaviors (as seen in Genentech, 1-800-GOT-JUNK, Land’s End, and others). Bliss also highlights the dangers of silos for the customer experience and advocates for organizational alignment, shared metrics, and a deliberate, memorable language around customers, culminating in her memorable metaphors like 'stairway to desire' and 'human duct tape.'
title: Silos to Service: Customer Experience Lessons from Jeanne Bliss
topics: land's end reliability and emotional packaging
